collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two siblings both want their late parent's canoe: share it, or let the one who needs it most have it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Since their mother died, (subject) and (friend) have not agreed on anything, and now they are arguing about her canoe. (subject) fishes every day and needs it. (friend) says their mother promised it to (friend.him/her) when (friend.he/she) was small, and it is all (friend.he/she) has of her. What should happen?

choices.label: Give It to Who Needs It

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They agree to share it: (subject) takes it fishing in the mornings, and (friend) paddles it out alone in the evenings, just to sit on the water where their mother used to. It works. Mostly. They still argue about who left the paddle on the beach.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The family decides (subject) should have it, because (subject.he/she) needs it to fish. (friend) accepts it, and does not speak to (subject) for a long time. Later, (subject) carves a small model of the canoe and leaves it at (friend)'s door. (friend) keeps it. They are speaking again, a little.
